column1: # <expected> is one of: allow | ask | deny
#   allow = the guard emits nothing and the normal permission flow applies.
# Rows are evaluated with NO repository policy file, so this table pins the
# framework's DEFAULT behaviour. Half of it is deliberately "allow": a guard
# that nags gets switched off within a day, and then it protects nothing.
# `bash -n` and an executable bit prove a hook runs, not that it is right. A
# hook that crashes exits non-zero, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking
# error, so a broken guard fails OPEN. This table is what prevents that.
# ── Ordinary engineering. None of these may ever prompt. ────────────────────
